decisions.reason: F4 incorrectly attributed a vector maximal inequality and matrix isometry directly to scalar interfaces. The needed bound follows by the elementary finite-sum inequality |sum_j a_j|² <= m sum_j |a_j|² and the scalar maximal bound, giving 4m times Frobenius energy. This routine coordinate derivation closes the gap without a new prerequisite or any change to the existence/uniqueness claim. The repair also corrects the Hölder exponent pair to (2,2).

F3/F9 silently extended scalar interfaces. A finite sum of scalar coordinate martingales gives the required martingale property, and the scalar isometry with |sum_j a_j|² <= m sum_j |a_j|² gives the sufficient matrix second-moment inequality. These are routine finite-coordinate derivations, now explicit; exact cross-coordinate isometry is unnecessary. Also made the digest concern explicit: resolvent growth and Gaussian increments give all fixed-mesh numerical moments by finite induction before the finite-energy maximal bound.

F1 attributed existence to a definition that explicitly disclaims it. F2 already supplies the global adapted continuous solution under the exact hypotheses and step 1.1 already cites F2, so this is a nonfatal attribution defect, now corrected. Also made the routine fixed-N fourth-supremum argument explicit so the finite expected square-energy hypothesis of F6 is checked before use; clarified predictable grid representatives.

reviews.reason: Checked the time-uniform cutoff Lipschitz bounds, applicability of global strong well-posedness, common-exit comparison, empty/initially-exited compacts, increasing exit times, and compatible-family uniqueness. Step 4.1 now derives the matrix estimate from scalar coordinate integrals, and applies Gronwall to a continuous integral majorant using finite path moments; stopped arbitrary local solutions have supremum bounded by |xi|+n. The Statement and AC assumption are unchanged. This is an author repair review, not independent acceptance of the repair.

Checked global dissipativity matches the full-space resolvent, common-noise conditional stability uses covariance hI, and finite numerical fourth moments license the martingale-product energy. Both endpoint increment bounds yield E|d|² <= Ch³, scalar-coordinate estimates yield E|xi_increment|² <= Ch E|e_n|²+Ch², and the L1 maximum bound plus Young absorption gives the stated discrete recurrence and Ch grid-maximum error. Claims, AC, and the restriction to grid error remain unchanged. This is an author repair review, not independent acceptance of the repair.

Checked F2 supplies existence and all exact moments, F3 supplies every uniform grid moment, and the interpolation has predictable integrand representatives. Polynomial drift growth and Brownian increments give delta second/fourth moments O(h)/O(h²) and squared taming defect O(h²). The one-sided drift bound gives the stated nonnegative error majorant; finite fixed-N fourth path moments license the L1 maximum inequality, Young absorbs v/2, and continuity plus Gronwall yields C_T h for the continuous supremum. Statement, dependencies and AC remain unchanged. This is an author repair review, not independent acceptance of the repair.
